subject.title: [优化建议] install.sh 模块化拆分以提升可维护性

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a modular `install.sh` architecture now, and if so what public entrypoint and helper-loading shape should be required?
rationale: This is not a broken current behavior; it changes the structure of a stable public setup surface whose docs, website sync, tests, and release validation currently assume one shell script.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded split
options.body: Approve a module layout only if `openclaw.ai/install.sh` remains a safe single entrypoint and the publish/test matrix is updated in the same plan.

options.title: Keep targeted refactors only
options.body: Leave this as backlog context and continue extracting or deleting installer sections only when tied to concrete bugs or validation improvements.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decide the served shell installer should remain monolithic to avoid helper-loading and `curl | bash` packaging risk.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded split
recommendation.body: Approve a module layout only if `openclaw.ai/install.sh` remains a safe single entrypoint and the publish/test matrix is updated in the same plan.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent installer-specific fixes and refactors make this the best available owner for deciding whether the split shape is worth the compatibility cost.
